# incident_alert_rules (Resource)

Read and replace the alert rules in your account.

Alert rules decide what happens to each alert: who is paged, where it is posted, and whether an incident is created. They are stored as sets: the organisation's required rules, its default rules, and one set per team. Each set is a list of blocks, and each block holds branches of conditions and actions.

A set of rules is one resource: its blocks, branches, actions and the expressions they reference
are written together on every apply.

An organisation has one set of `required` rules and one of `default` rules, and a plan that creates
either fails once it exists. To manage one, import it by ID. Destroying it afterwards empties the set and hands
it back to the dashboard. Each team has at most one set of `team` rules, which is created and deleted like
any other resource. A set's kind cannot change, so a plan that changes `kind` fails, and changing
`team_id` replaces the set.

Writing alert rules needs your organisation to have moved to alert rules. Until then the API refuses to
create, update or delete a set, and this resource fails at apply with that message.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Each team has one set of team rules, which run for the team's alerts. Teams are catalog
# entries of your Team type, so look the team up rather than hardcoding its ID.
data "incident_catalog_type" "team" {
  name = "Team"
}

data "incident_catalog_entry" "platform" {
  catalog_type_id = data.incident_catalog_type.team.id
  identifier      = "Platform"
}

data "incident_escalation_path" "platform" {
  name = "Platform"
}

resource "incident_alert_rules" "platform" {
  kind    = "team"
  team_id = data.incident_catalog_entry.platform.id

  # Blocks that don't name their own alert message template post with this one.
  message_template = { value_literal = "01KHJTJR4FZJJZQ6G02EBFJAAY" }

  # Every block runs for an alert. The first branch runs when its conditions hold, and a
  # second branch, with no conditions, runs when they don't.
  block {
    id = "database-alerts"

    # Overrides the set's message template for this block.
    message_template = { value_literal = "01KHJTM5Q8N3RZ7XW2D4FBCYVA" }

    branch {
      id = "database"
      condition_groups = [{
        conditions = [{
          subject        = "alert.title"
          operation      = "contains"
          param_bindings = [{ value_literal = "database" }]
        }]
      }]

      actions = [
        {
          id       = "page-platform"
          type     = "escalate"
          escalate = { escalation_paths = { values = [data.incident_escalation_path.platform.id] } }
        },
        {
          id              = "declare-incident"
          type            = "create_incident"
          create_incident = {}
        },
      ]
    }

    branch {
      id = "everything-else"
      actions = [{
        id   = "post-to-channel"
        type = "post_slack"
        post_slack = {
          channels = { values = ["C01234567"] }
          mode     = "per_alert"
        }
      }]
    }
  }
}

# An organisation has one set of required rules, which run for every alert, and one of
# default rules, which run when no team's rules ran. Creating either fails once it exists,
# so import an existing set to manage it. Destroying it empties the set and hands it back
# to the dashboard.
import {
  to = incident_alert_rules.required
  id = "01FCNDV6P870EA6S7TK1DSYDG0"
}

resource "incident_alert_rules" "required" {
  kind = "required"

  block {
    id = "investigate"

    branch {
      id      = "always"
      actions = [{ id = "start-investigation", type = "investigate" }]
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) Which set this is. Required rules run for every alert. Team rules run for the alert's team. Default rules run when no team's rules ran. Possible values are: `required`, `team`, `default`. A set's kind cannot change.

### Optional

- `block` (Block List) The blocks of rules, in order. Every block runs for an alert. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--block))
- `message_template` (Attributes) The alert message template for blocks without their own: its ID, or a reference. Leave it out to post the default message. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--message_template))
- `named_expression` (Block List) An expression this resource owns, addressed by name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--named_expression))
- `team_id` (String) The catalog entry ID of the team, set only for team rules, and required for them.
- `unlock_in_dashboard` (Boolean) Whether to leave this resource unlocked in the incident.io dashboard, so people can edit it there. Defaults to `false`: Terraform claims what it manages, and a claimed resource cannot be edited in the dashboard. Set it to `true` to leave the resource unclaimed — pair that with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [...] }` naming the attributes people edit, or the next apply reverts them. Setting it on a resource Terraform already claimed hands that resource back, and someone disconnecting one in the dashboard shows as no change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this set of rules
- `version` (Number) The current version number. Every update writes the next version.

<a id="nestedblock--block"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block`

Required:

- `id` (String) Identifier for this block, unique within the set. Choose a readable key and send the same one on every update, so the block keeps its identity.

Optional:

- `branch` (Block List) One or two branches: an if branch, and optionally an else branch with no condition groups (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--block--branch))
- `message_template` (Attributes) The alert message template for this block, in place of the set's: its ID, or a reference. Leave it out to use the set's template. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--message_template))

<a id="nestedblock--block--branch"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch`

Required:

- `id` (String) Identifier for this branch, unique within the set. Choose a readable key and send the same one on every update: alert groups are keyed on it.

Optional:

- `actions` (Attributes List) The actions to take when the branch holds (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions))
- `branch` (Block List) Branches nested one level deep. Each runs when this branch ran and its own conditions hold, and cannot nest further. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--block--branch--branch))
- `condition_groups` (Attributes List) The branch holds when every condition in any one group holds. A branch with no groups always holds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--condition_groups))

<a id="nestedatt--block--branch--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch.actions`

Required:

- `type` (String) Which action to take. Set the attribute of the same name with its parameters. `investigate` has none. Possible values are: `escalate`, `post_slack`, `post_microsoft_teams`, `create_incident`, `investigate`.

Optional:

- `create_incident` (Attributes) Create an incident from the alert, or attach it to the incident its group already has. Set when type is `create_incident`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident))
- `escalate` (Attributes) Page escalation paths or users about the alert. Set escalation_paths, users, or both. Set when type is `escalate`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--escalate))
- `id` (String) Identifier for this action, unique within the set. Leave it out and the server assigns a new one on every apply, which Terraform doesn't store.
- `post_microsoft_teams` (Attributes) Post the alert to Microsoft Teams channels. Set when type is `post_microsoft_teams`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--post_microsoft_teams))
- `post_slack` (Attributes) Post the alert to Slack channels. Set when type is `post_slack`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--post_slack))

<a id="nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch.actions.create_incident`

Optional:

- `auto_decline` (Boolean) Decline the incident if its alerts resolve before anyone accepts it. Defaults to false.
- `incident_template` (Attributes) The incident template to create from: its ID, or a reference. Leave it out to use the organisation's default template. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident--incident_template))
- `is_private` (Boolean) Create the incident as private. A private alert, or a template whose incident type allows only private incidents, makes it private anyway. Defaults to false.
- `membership_teams` (Attributes) The teams whose members can see the incident and join its channel when it is private: team catalog entry IDs in `values`, or a reference. Leave it out to use the template's teams. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident--membership_teams))

<a id="nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident--incident_template"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch.actions.create_incident.incident_template`

Optional:

- `array_value` (Attributes List) Several values, spelled out. Needed when they mix fixed values and references. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident--incident_template--array_value))
- `expression_ref` (String) The name of a named_expression in this resource, whose result becomes the value.
- `value` (Attributes) One value, spelled out. `value_literal` and `value_reference` are shorthand for this. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--create_incident--incident_template--value))
- `value_literal` (String) A fixed value. A catalog entry ID is a literal, not a reference.
- `value_reference` (String) A reference into the scope, such as `payload.team`.
- `values` (List of String) Several fixed values. For a mix of fixed values and references, use array_value.

<a id="nestedatt--block--branch--actions--escalate"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch.actions.escalate`

Optional:

- `auto_cancel` (Boolean) Cancel the escalation when the alert resolves, or when every alert in its group resolves. Defaults to false.
- `escalation_paths` (Attributes) The escalation paths to page: escalation path IDs in `values`, or an `expression_ref` that finds them, such as from the alert's team. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--escalate--escalation_paths))
- `grace_period_seconds` (Number) How long an alert that joins a group with a live page waits before it pages. 0, the default, pages at once. Only used with on_each_new_alert. Allowed with on_priority_increase, which ignores it.
- `mode` (String) How an alert that joins a group pages. on_each_new_alert pages for every alert. on_priority_increase pages a target only when the alert's priority is above every live page the group already has to that target. Defaults to on_each_new_alert. Possible values are: `on_priority_increase`, `on_each_new_alert`.
- `urgency` (Attributes) The urgency to page at: the ID of an escalation urgency catalog entry, or a reference. Leave it out to page at the alert priority's default urgency. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--escalate--urgency))
- `users` (Attributes) The users to page: user IDs in `values`, or a reference. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--actions--escalate--users))

<a id="nestedatt--block--branch--actions--post_microsoft_teams"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch.actions.post_microsoft_teams`

Required:

<a id="nestedatt--block--branch--branch--actions--escalate"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block.branch.branch.actions.escalate`

Optional:

- `auto_cancel` (Boolean) Cancel the escalation when the alert resolves, or when every alert in its group resolves. Defaults to false.
- `escalation_paths` (Attributes) The escalation paths to page: escalation path IDs in `values`, or an `expression_ref` that finds them, such as from the alert's team. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--branch--actions--escalate--escalation_paths))
- `grace_period_seconds` (Number) How long an alert that joins a group with a live page waits before it pages. 0, the default, pages at once. Only used with on_each_new_alert. Allowed with on_priority_increase, which ignores it.
- `mode` (String) How an alert that joins a group pages. on_each_new_alert pages for every alert. on_priority_increase pages a target only when the alert's priority is above every live page the group already has to that target. Defaults to on_each_new_alert. Possible values are: `on_priority_increase`, `on_each_new_alert`.
- `urgency` (Attributes) The urgency to page at: the ID of an escalation urgency catalog entry, or a reference. Leave it out to page at the alert priority's default urgency. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--branch--actions--escalate--urgency))
- `users` (Attributes) The users to page: user IDs in `values`, or a reference. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block--branch--branch--actions--escalate--users))

<a id="nestedblock--named_expression--operation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `named_expression.operation`

Optional:

- `branches` (Block, Optional) A lookup table, evaluated in order until one matches. Must be the only operation in its expression, with start_from = ".". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--named_expression--operation--branches))
- `cast` (Attributes) Converts the current value to another type. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--cast))
- `concatenate` (Attributes) Adds the values behind another reference to the current value, keeping each value once. There is no delimiter, despite the name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--concatenate))
- `count` (Attributes) Counts the values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--count))
- `filter` (Attributes) Keeps the values matching these conditions. Inside a filter the value under test is bound as `input`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--filter))
- `first` (Attributes) Takes the first value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--first))
- `max` (Attributes) Takes the largest value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--max))
- `min` (Attributes) Takes the smallest value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--min))
- `navigate` (Attributes) Follows an attribute of the current value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--navigate))
- `parse` (Attributes) Evaluates a function against the current value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--parse))
- `random` (Attributes) Takes one value at random. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--random))
- `sum` (Attributes) Adds the values together. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--named_expression--operation--sum))

## Import

Import is supported using an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) or the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import):

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash

# Import a set of alert rules using its ID. Replace the ID with a real ID from your
# incident.io organization: the public API's list endpoint returns each set with its kind
# and team. Creating the organization's required or default rules fails once they exist,
# so this is how Terraform takes them over. Copy each action's id from state into your
# configuration after the import, or the next apply updates the set once to drop them.
terraform import incident_alert_rules.example 01ABC123DEF456GHI789JKL
```
